text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today despite a week of gains, as oil prices—the main driver of the company's earnings—gave back some ground after a sharp run-up. US crude closed at $97.26 per barrel, down from $109.51 globally, suggesting some profit-taking after the stock climbed 4.85% over the past two weeks on the back of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and supply disruptions, including Saudi Arabia's shutdown of a critical pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz.

The broader energy sector remains supported by multiple tailwinds: Trump administration policies repealing climate regulations that had constrained fossil fuel expansion, along with market expectations for higher gas prices as US-Iran tensions persist and the Russia-Ukraine conflict continues to disrupt global energy supplies. Today's small pullback fits a pattern of consolidation after a strong run rather than a fundamental shift in the outlook for oil prices or producer profits.
